To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current state of affairs is unsatisfactory, that there is a need for standardization of terminology interchange formats at various levels, that a new generation of interchange formats has been proposed, and that this new generation is being implemented in the SALT terminology management system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and applying methods and techniques that will enable the integration of terminological resources in a multilingual and multi-domain context.
the development of an integrated, interoperable framework for the interchange, sharing and management of terminological data, which will be based on the principles of openness and extensibility.
the development of a new approach to the integration of terminological resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problems of accessibility of multilingual terminological data are far from being solved and that the situation is getting worse rather than better.
the current situation is one of chaos and confusion and the future prospects are bleak unless a concerted effort to develop an international standard for terminology exchange is undertaken.
there is still a long way to go before we have the kind of interoperability and integration that we would need to achieve our goal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are in the process of creating a new type of terminological resource, a ‘multilingual terminological database’ (MTDB) which is a combination of a terminological database and a terminology resource.
we have been working towards a new approach to the development of standards, and we have developed a set of standards that are based on a new approach.
we have developed a set of standards for the exchange and sharing of terminological resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a higher degree of integration is needed in order to achieve a more seamless access to multilingual terminological knowledge.
a new generation of standards is needed to address the current lack of compatibility among existing terminological resources.
the lack of co-operation among the different communities involved in the development of multilingual terminology resources is a major obstacle to progress.
